findings.issue: The A-5 skip guard `if (pots.length <= 1 && levels.length <= 1) return null` is only exercised with pots.length >= 2. No test covers one pot while contributions make several levels, which is exactly what the pre-TASK-1.10 single-pot engine would produce. So if the guard regresses the checker would wave that engine through.
findings.evidence: Mutation run in a throwaway copy: changing the guard to `pots.length <= 1 || levels.length <= 1`, or to `pots.length <= 1`, left every test in tests/engine and tests/playtest passing. The only failures were the same 10 environment-only failures as the unmutated copy (missing tools/ dir). All SPEC-09 crafted cases (a)-(e) have 2 or 3 pots.
findings.fix: Add case (f) to side-pot-invariants: S1turn with pots collapsed to [{amount: 104, eligible: [1,2,3,4]}] should give exactly one pot-eligibility violation, 'there are 1 pots but contributions make 3'. The test file is locked, so this needs a spec amendment or a follow-up task.

findings.issue: In potStructureMessage, `level` is each seat's capped completed contribution (the spec's c(p)) and `levels` is the distinct sorted pot levels. Names that differ by one letter make P7 and P8 hard to read: `level[...] < at` versus `levels[k]`.
findings.evidence: const level = put.map((c) => Math.min(c, second)); const levels = [...new Set(level.filter(...))]

summary: The engine side pots are correct. I checked buildPots layering, including folded dead money (the last pot is uncapped), the TASK-1.9 return being subtracted before levels are built, per-pot best-hand award with splitPot odd chips, payOut summing shares across awards, and fold-out (always one level). I also ran an inline fuzz in a throwaway copy: 260,000 random hands with 2-10 seats, $5-$192 stacks and SB 1 or 2, run with checkState after every step and checkStep on every action. Each hand's awards were compared exactly against an independent oracle that rebuilds levels from totalContribution capped at the second-highest and pays each pot to its best eligible hand(s) via splitPot. There were 0 mismatches and 0 violations. The run covered 29,331 multi-pot hands, 2,686 hands with tied pots, 953 odd-chip ties and 9,337 side pots with one eligible seat. No fold-out ever had more than one pot, as the spec predicts. Engine mutations (folded seats counted as levels, ignoring pot eligibility at showdown, payOut taking only the first share, not subtracting the return, `>` instead of `>=`, min instead of max for best hand, no tie split) were all caught by the new tests. The one survivor, capping the last pot, is equivalent because the spec's defensive uncapped last pot can't be reached. The checker (P6-P8) imports only types and legalActions from the engine and recomputes levels itself. Its cap at the second-highest completed contribution matches the engine's return in every reachable state. The skip guard is equivalent to the existing checks for one pot and one level. However, the half of the guard covering 'one pot but several levels' has no test (MINOR). Locked tests are unchanged and the new tests pass. Lint and typecheck pass, and the 10,000-hand playtest output is byte-identical to the baseline. No files under src/ui, src/table, src/advice or e2e were touched. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
